author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing treats a page before the first as the first page
summary: A request for the owner listing that names a page below the first shows the first page of matches instead of the error page. The rule applies whether or not the request also names a last name.
acceptance_criteria: given an owner listing request naming page zero, when the listing runs, then the first page of matches is shown
given an owner listing request naming a negative page, when the listing runs, then the first page of matches is shown
given an owner listing request naming any page before the first, when the listing runs, then the error page is not shown
given an owner listing request naming a page before the first, when the request also names a last name, then it behaves the same as without one
non_goals: the veterinarian directory's handling of a page before the first
page values that are not numbers
page values beyond the last page
notes: Owner statement quoted in the intake-decision at line 1; intake recorded no further decisions. Scoped to the owner listing only, which is the surface the report names. The veterinarian directory shares the same paging shape but was not reported, so it stays out and is recorded as an open question in docs/prd.md, alongside non-numeric page values. Requirement added to the Owner records section of docs/prd.md, marked confirmed 2026-08-17; it refines the paged listing of REQ-OWN-002 and contradicts no existing requirement or Non-Goals row. Edge case 4 of Owner records covers the last-name variant. Single deliverable surface (code plus its tests); small but standalone, with no sibling slice to batch it with.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Durable memory already covers this surface unchanged. The `OwnerController` Contracts row in docs/system-design.md owns the paged owner search, and the Constants section already records that page size is a local variable in that controller's pagination helper. The defect is one line inside that helper: `findPaginatedForOwnersLastName` passes `page - 1` straight to `PageRequest.of`, so any page below the first yields a negative index and the framework's IllegalArgumentException reaches the error page (confirmed by reading src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/OwnerController.java:133-137 in full; the IDE oracle is not connected in this run, so the basis is a direct source read rather than a symbol resolution). The fix normalizes the request parameter to the first page at the web boundary, which is exactly the security-principles.md trust-boundary rule for arriving external input (validate range before use) and stays inside the architecture-principles.md Web controller row: binding and normalizing the request, not adding a business rule. No new type, package, pattern, or dependency. The only docs/ write is the requirement id joining the `OwnerController` Contracts row, with the row's purpose extended to name the normalization.
integration_points: the private pagination helper in OwnerController is the single call site converting the one-based page parameter to a zero-based PageRequest; normalization belongs there or at the parameter itself, before the conversion
addPaginationModel publishes currentPage to owners/ownersList — a normalized page must reach the model as the first page so the rendered pager is self-consistent

patterns.description: existing one-based-page to zero-based-PageRequest conversion in findPaginatedForOwnersLastName; the clamp goes on this path, keeping page size and repository call untouched
external input arrives: validate range and shape before use — the request parameter is the boundary, the controller is where the check belongs

risks.risk: the clamp is generalized to VetController, whose paged listing has the same shape but is a declared non-goal for this slice and an open question in docs/prd.md
risks.mitigation: keep the change inside OwnerController; the veterinarian directory stays untouched and its open question stays open

risks.risk: a shared normalization helper is extracted across the owner and vet controllers to look tidy, coupling two packages that do not reference each other today and breaking the acyclic graph recorded in docs/system-design.md § Package Structure
risks.mitigation: no extraction in this slice — the fix is local to one private helper

risks.risk: the clamp is read as a business rule and taken as licence to extend the recorded controller-rules deviation
risks.mitigation: it is input normalization at the HTTP boundary, which the Web controller row admits; no domain decision moves into the controller

risks.risk: a non-numeric page value is folded in while touching the same parameter
risks.mitigation: explicitly out of scope per the prd-entry non-goals and PRD open question; binding failure behavior is unchanged

notes: No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is a no-op. This defect is not listed in docs/system-design.md § Known Defects (that table is the 2026-07-31 survey set, all still unfixed), and it is not added there — the slice removes the behavior rather than recording it as standing. Terms follow docs/ubiquitous-language.md: Owner for the person, veterinarian directory for the vet listing.

author: change-grader
summary: clamp the owner listing page parameter to the first page

blast_radius.note: One production file in one module (OwnerController), plus its test and two docs rows; no sensitive paths, no shared helper extracted, and VetController's identical paging shape is deliberately untouched.

semantic_surprise.note: Read all four production hunks: Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) is applied once and the clamped requestedPage is threaded to both the repository query and the pager model, so query and rendered currentPage stay in sync; the FIRST_PAGE constant substitution in the defaultValue and in page - FIRST_PAGE is behavior-identical to the literal 1, and no upper bound, binding, or single-result redirect path changed.

test_adequacy.note: The three new MockMvc tests would fail against a broken implementation -- removing the clamp restores PageRequest.of(-1) and breaks status().isOk() -- and the ArgumentCaptor on the Pageable asserts the zero-based index actually reaching the repository, which distinguishes a real fix from a display-only one that merely sets currentPage.
